title: Overview
lead: What you should not miss in your latest statement, in one place.
leadForecast: My forecast for your {{month}} statement is <c>{{amount}}</c>. Of that, <m>{{installments}}</m> is already fixed by installments.
noStatements: Upload your first statement and follow your installments, spending and the things to watch from here.
pending: Writing the commentary. This can take 10 to 60 seconds.
none: I haven’t commented on this statement yet.
sentData: Only the date, description, amount, currency and type of each transaction go to the tool you chose.
noProvider: Choose a tool first to get a commentary.
noCites: This point is not tied to one transaction.
disclaimer: Code computes the totals and installments; the model only adds categories and commentary.

first.lead: Once you upload a card statement, I show the forecast for the next one, the alerts and your installment load here.
first.title: Start in two steps
first.label: Getting started
first.uploadBody: Pick the bank’s PDF statement. The file stays on this computer; code reads the amounts and installments.
first.aiTitle: If you like, pick a tool for commentary
first.aiBody: For categories and commentary I use an AI tool on your computer. Installments and the forecast work without one.

forecast.title: Next statement
forecast.description: Forecast for the {{month}} statement. Installments are certain; I count subscriptions at their last amount and variable spend at the median of earlier months.
forecast.installmentsNote: Installments that fall in this month
forecast.subscriptionsNone: No subscriptions in the last month
forecast.openPeriod: Spend you added by hand or by import since the {{from}} cut-off: <m>{{amount}}</m>.
forecast.openPeriodNone: You haven’t added any spend since the {{from}} cut-off.
forecast.backtest: I tested this method on {{count}} past months: the forecast was off by <m>{{mae}}</m> on average ({{mape}} percent), mostly too {{direction}}.
forecast.backtestNoPct: I tested this method on {{count}} past months: the forecast was off by <m>{{mae}}</m> on average, mostly too {{direction}}.
forecast.backtestEven: I tested this method on {{count}} past months: the forecast was off by <m>{{mae}}</m> on average.
forecast.backtestNone: I can’t test the forecast yet. That needs at least {{need}} months of statements.
forecast.backtestCaption: Each month was forecast from earlier data only.
forecast.loadError: I couldn’t get the forecast. The back end may be off.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.label: Alerts
alerts.unknown: There is an alert this version does not know.

installment_ending.title: Last installment of {{description}}
installment_ending.detail: The {{month}} statement has the last installment: <m>{{amount}}</m>. From the month after, you no longer pay it.

limit_high.title: Your limit is nearly used up
limit_high.detail: The statement total is <m>{{total}}</m> and the card limit <m>{{limit}}</m>. You have used {{share}} percent of it.

fee_charged.title: A fee was charged
fee_charged.detail: The {{month}} statement has <m>{{total}}</m> of fees. If it is the annual card fee, you can ask for it back.

tax_charged.title: Taxes were charged
tax_charged.detail: The {{month}} statement has <m>{{total}}</m> of BSMV and KKDF.

foreign_currency.title: Spend in a foreign currency
foreign_currency.detail: On the {{month}} statement, spend in {{currencies}} came to <m>{{total}}</m>.

missing_statement.title: A statement is missing
missing_statement.detail: The {{month}} statement of {{card}} is missing. Installment and spend totals for that month are incomplete.

subscription_price_rise.title: {{merchant}} went up
subscription_price_rise.detail: The charge went from <m>{{previous}}</m> to <m>{{last}}</m>, up {{change}} percent.

due_soon.title: Payment due {{date}}
due_soon.detail: The statement balance is <m>{{total}}</m>; the minimum payment is <m>{{minimum}}</m>.

statement_overdue.title: The {{card}} statement is late
statement_overdue.detail: The cut-off should have been {{date}}. Upload the statement and the forecast and alerts update.

charged_after_cancel.title: {{merchant}} charged after you cancelled
charged_after_cancel.detail: You marked it cancelled on {{date}}; <m>{{total}}</m> was charged after that. You can dispute it with your bank.

load.title: Installments over 12 months
load.sentence: Installments fall in {{busy}} of the next 12 months. The heaviest month is {{month}}, at <m>{{amount}}</m>.
load.sentenceNone: No installments in the next 12 months.
load.loadError: I couldn’t get the installment plan.
